Popover from ui-components shows a bubble with an arrow pointing at the button that opened it, telling more about it: a title and a text, or components of the page. The server shows it in the response to the click, so what it says can come from the server just then. It closes with its ×, Escape, a click outside it or a click on the button again, and gives the focus back to the button; it follows the button as the page scrolls.

It opens where you ask: on any side of the button, centered on it or along it from either edge, or on the side with the most room. Without room on its side it opens on the other one, and it slides to stay in the window, its arrow still pointing at the button. Nine designs, from a card with a stripe of its color to glass, neon or a comic speech bubble, each in five variants, take their colors from the theme, light or dark. The gallery draws each design open where its Position drop-down says, and Open it opens it there for real.

A popover can show any component: the facts below are rendered by the server as the popover opens, and the form renaming the project is a Wicket form in a popover, its error shown in it. React and Svelte render their own content into it. Everything works under a strict Content Security Policy, without inline style.

Each button opens a popover on its side of the target: from one edge, centered, or from the other edge; the one in the middle opens where there is most room. Scroll the page with one open and watch it follow, or flip to the other side.
